I am 45 years old, I only finished primary school, and I have been farming these fields for 20 years. Everything I know I learned from doing it myself and watching my neighbors. My family has 7 mouths to feed, so I cannot afford a bad year.

I have 10.1 mu in total. I grow wheat and maize on 8 mu — that is my main cropping system, wheat in winter and maize right after harvest in summer. I keep 2.1 mu for cotton because cotton brings cash, and we need cash for school fees and medicine.

For wheat, I buy an improved variety from the seed dealer in town. Last year I got about 500 kg per mu, and my neighbor who put a bit more fertilizer did a little better, so this year I will do the same. I rotary till after the maize comes off. Before planting in October, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that gives me about 11 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potassium per mu. Then I add urea for nitrogen, about 35 kg per mu total. I split it: half at planting, half at jointing in spring when the wheat turns a bit yellow. I irrigate three times: once in winter before the deep cold, once at jointing, and once at heading. I spray four times total — herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once because last year there was a bit of rust. I expect 500 kg per mu if the frost does not hit too hard.

For maize, I plant Denghai hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in June. There is barely one week between harvest and planting, so I do not till — I plant directly into the wheat stubble. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 12 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once when the leaves are big, and once at grain filling. I spray three times for insects and weeds. I expect about 525 kg per mu.

Cotton is on my other 2.1 mu. I rotary till that plot in April and plant an improved cotton variety. I put about 10 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs a lot of spraying — I spray 13 times through the season because the bollworm never gives up. I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll setting. I expect about 275 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Every kilo of fertilizer costs real money. I would rather use a little too much than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I have learned to live with.
